facts.statement: Stenopterygius fossils date from the Toarcian to the Aalenian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Toarcian-Aalenian~

facts.statement: The genus Stenopterygius was described by Otto Jaekel in 1904.
facts.quote: authority: Jaekel, 1904

facts.statement: The type species of Stenopterygius is Ichthyosaurus quadriscissus.
facts.quote: type_species: Ichthyosaurus quadriscissus

facts.statement: Species within the genus include S. triscissus, S. longipes, and S. aaleniensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: *S. triscissus Quenstedt, 1856 [originally Ichthyosaurus] S. longipes Wurstemberger, 1876 S. aaleniensis Maxwell et al., 2012

facts.statement: Stenopterygius was a medium-sized ichthyosaur that likely had a warm-blooded metabolism and blubber.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized ichthyosaur, with multiple well-preserved specimens, including one which preserved evidence of countershading (similar to most sharks), blubber and a raised, homeothermic metabolism.

facts.statement: A female Stenopterygius fossil that died in childbirth suggests the species gave birth tail-first, similar to modern whales.
facts.quote: as well as a female specimen that died in childbirth that showed that the genus preferred tail-first births similar to modern cetaceans.

facts.statement: Stenopterygius fossils have been found in England, France, Germany, Luxembourg, and Switzerland.
facts.quote: known from Europe (England, France, Germany, Luxembourg and Switzerland)

facts.statement: S. quadriscissus and S. triscissus reached a maximum length of about 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: Stenopterygius was a medium-sized ichthyosaur, with S. quadriscissus and S. triscissus reaching a maximum length of about 3.5 m

facts.statement: The species S. uniter could exceed 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: while the larger S. uniter could exceed 4 m

facts.statement: Young adult S. triscissus reached at least 2 meters in length, with the type specimen measuring 2.2 meters.
facts.quote: Young adults reached at least 2 m long, as indicated by the type specimen of S. triscissus measuring 2.2 m long

facts.statement: The skull of Stenopterygius ended in a beak-like structure filled with many large teeth.
facts.quote: Its skull was extended into a kind of a beak and was armed with a quantity of large teeth

facts.statement: Stenopterygius had a large, semicircular, leathery vertical tail fin and a triangular dorsal fin.
facts.quote: The tail terminated in a large, semicircular, leathery, vertical caudal fin and even a triangular dorsal fin was present

facts.statement: Preserved skin traces revealed that Stenopterygius had countershading, being darker on its back than its belly.
facts.quote: One well-preserved fossil of Stenopterygius preserves traces of skin, from which the animal's coloration was discovered to be countershaded (darker on the back than the underbelly)

facts.statement: Michael W. Maisch redescribed most of the over 100 known Stenopterygius specimens in 2008.
facts.quote: Most of the more than 100 known specimens of Stenopterygius were redescribed by Michael W. Maisch in 2008

facts.statement: Maisch considered Ichthyosaurus triscissus to be a valid species of Stenopterygius, following Woodward's 1932 work.
facts.quote: Maisch followed Woodward (1932) and considered Ichthyosaurus triscissus to be a valid species of Stenopterygius

facts.statement: The lectotype of Stenopterygius is a complete skeleton (GPIT 43/0219-1) that preserved a very large embryo.
facts.quote: Stenopterygius is known from the lectotype GPIT 43/0219-1 (also registered as GPIT-PV-30028 and PV 7532), a complete, articulated skeleton which preserved a very large embryo

facts.statement: The type specimen of Stenopterygius dates to the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, approximately 182 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, about 182 million years ago

facts.statement: A 2010 analysis by Druckenmiller and Maxwell provided a cladogram topology for Stenopterygius.
facts.quote: The cladogram below follows the topology from a 2010 analysis by Patrick S. Druckenmiller and Erin E. Maxwell

facts.statement: Stenopterygius lived in the open sea and hunted fish, cephalopods, and other animals, similar to modern dolphins.
facts.quote: The habits of Stenopterygius spp. were similar to those of present-day dolphins. They spent most of their lives in the open sea, where they hunted fish, cephalopods, and other animals

facts.statement: Abdominal cavities of Stenopterygius skeletons often contain remains of food.
facts.quote: The abdominal cavities of skeletons of this ichthyosaur often contain the remains of such food

facts.statement: A famous Stenopterygius fossil shows a mother and baby that died during childbirth, proving ichthyosaurs were viviparous.
facts.quote: One famous fossil is that of a mother and baby that died in childbirth (ichthyosaurs were viviparous)

facts.statement: Some Stenopterygius specimens contain fetuses suggesting that head-first birth also occurred.
facts.quote: However, there are specimens known with fetuses in utero suggesting a head-first birth

facts.statement: A 2018 report found evidence of blubber in a Stenopterygius specimen, indicating it was warm-blooded.
facts.quote: In 2018, a Stenopterygius specimen was reported with evidence of having had blubber, which indicates that other ichthyosaurs and it were homeothermic ("warm blooded")

facts.statement: Stenopterygius was an extinct ichthyosaur that lived during the Early to Middle Jurassic (Toarcian to Aalenian) in Europe, including England, France, Germany, Switzerland, and Luxembourg.
facts.quote: Stenopterygius (gr. aleta estrecha) es un género extinto de ictiosaurio del Jurásico temprano y medio (Toarciano - Aaleniense) que vivió en Europa (Inglaterra, Francia, Alemania, Suiza y Luxemburgo).

facts.statement: The maximum total length of Stenopterygius was 4 meters.
facts.quote: Su longitud total máxima era de 4 metros.

facts.statement: More than 100 known specimens of Stenopterygius were recently redescribed by Michael W. Maisch.
facts.quote: Muchos de los ejemplares conocidos de Stenopterygius, más de 100, fueron recientemente redescritos por Michael W. Maisch.

facts.statement: Many specimens previously referred to Stenopterygius hauffianus were reassigned to the separate genus Hauffiopteryx.
facts.quote: Esta especie fue reasignada a su propio género, Hauffiopteryx.

facts.statement: Stenopterygius is known from the lectotype GPIT 43/0219-1, a complete skeleton that preserves a very large embryo.
facts.quote: Stenopterygius es conocido por el lectotipo GPIT 43/0219-1, un esqueleto completo el cual preserva un embrión muy grande.

facts.statement: A specimen measuring about 3.15 meters long was found in the Posidonia Shale at Holzmaden, dating to the early Toarcian of the Lower Jurassic, approximately 182 million years ago.
facts.quote: El animal medía cerca de 3.15 metros de largo. Fue encontrado en la subzona de los ammonites Harpoceras elegantulum-exaratum (más específicamente Lias ε II3-4), la zona Harpoceras falcifer del conocido lagerstätte del Esquisto de Posidonia en Holzmaden, datando de principios del Toarciano en el Jurásico Inferior, hace cerca de 182 millones de años.

facts.statement: The species S. triscissus is known from the holotype GPIT 12/0224-2, a nearly complete articulated skeleton of a subadult measuring about 2.1 meters long.
facts.quote: S. triscissus es conocido a partir del holotipo GPIT 12/0224-2, un esqueleto casi completo y articulado. El animal es un adulto joven de cerca de 2.1 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The species S. uniter is known from the holotype SMNS 14216, a complete articulated skeleton of an adult measuring about 3.35 meters long, which was destroyed in World War II.
facts.quote: S. uniter es conocido del holotipo SMNS 14216, un esqueleto articulado completo que fue destruido en la Segunda Guerra Mundial. El animal era un adulto de cerca de 3.35 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Additional materials were described by Hannah Caine and Michael J. Benton in 2011 from the early Toarcian of Strawberry Bank, Ilminster, England.
facts.quote: Materiales adicionales fueron descritos por Hannah Caine y Michael J. Benton en 2011, de principios del Toarciano de Strawberry Bank, Ilminster en Inglaterra.

facts.statement: A new species, Stenopterygius aaleniensis, from the Middle Jurassic of southwest Germany was described in 2012.
facts.quote: Una nueva especie del Jurásico Medio del suroeste de Alemania, Stenopterygius aaleniensis, fue descrita en 2012.

facts.statement: Research results indicate that the family Stenopterygiidae is monotypic, including only the type genus Stenopterygius.
facts.quote: Estos resultados significan que Stenopterygiidae es una familia monotípica que incluye solo al género tipo Stenopterygius.

facts.statement: Stenopterygius was physically similar to the well-known Ichthyosaurus but had a smaller skull and narrower flippers.
facts.quote: Stenopterygius era físicamente similar al mejor conocido Ichthyosaurus, pero tenía un cráneo menor y aletas más estrechas.

facts.statement: Its skull extended into a long snout and was armed with numerous large teeth.
facts.quote: Su cráneo se extendía en un largo morro y estaba armado con una cantidad de grandes dientes.

facts.statement: Stenopterygius had habits similar to modern dolphins, spending much of its life in open waters hunting fish, cephalopods, and other animals.
facts.quote: Los hábitos de Stenopterygius eran similares a los de los delfines de hoy en día. Pasaba mucha de su vida en el mar abierto, donde cazaba peces, cefalópodos y otros animales.

facts.statement: The abdominal cavities of Stenopterygius skeletons frequently contain the remains of its food.
facts.quote: La cavidad abdominal de los esqueletos de este ictiosaurio frecuentemente contienen los restos de sus comidas.

facts.statement: A famous fossil represents a mother and her baby that died during birth, proving that ichthyosaurs were viviparous.
facts.quote: Un famoso fósil representa a una madre y su bebé que murieron en el parto (los ictiosaurios eran vivíparos).

facts.statement: This proved that young ichthyosaurs were born with their tails emerging first, just like cetaceans, to prevent drowning before leaving the birth canal.
facts.quote: Esto probó que los ictiosaurios jóvenes nacían sacando primero su cola, precisamente como los cétaceos, para evitar que se ahogaran antes de salir del canal de parto.

facts.statement: In 2018, a Stenopterygius specimen was found with evidence of fat similar to that of cetaceans, indicating the animal, and thus all ichthyosaurs, were homeothermic.
facts.quote: En 2018, un ejemplar de Stenopterygius fue hallado con evidencia de haber presentado grasa parecida a la de los cetáceos, lo cual indica que el animal, y por tanto, todos los ictiosaurios, eran homeotermos.

facts.statement: The time range for Stenopterygius is from the Toarcian to the Aalenian, between 184.2 and 170.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Aalenian (184.2 to 170.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A 2026 study interpreted S. uniter as a junior synonym of S. longipes and Magnipterygius huenei as a junior synonym of S. quadriscissus.
rejected.quote: A 2026 study, which analyzed fossils from the Early Jurassic (Toarcian) Whitby Mudstone Formation interpreted S. uniter as a junior synonym of S. longipes and interpreting Magnipterygius huenei as a junior synonym of S. quadriscissus

rejected.quote: Stenopterygius era un veloz nadador, con una velocidad de crucero similar a la de un atún, el cual está entre los más veloces de los peces vivientes.

rejected.quote: Biot et al. (2026) describe a specimen of Stenopterygius quadriscissus from the Toarcian strata of the Whitby Mudstone Formation (United Kingdom) and revise the species of the genus Stenopterygius.
